test_title: PYST 28: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 21 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the primary purpose of introducing e-passports in India in May 2025?

options.text: To enhance security and prevent identity fraud
To reduce the cost of passport production
To increase the number of pages in the passport
To change the colour of the passport cover

solution:
The correct answer is __**To enhance security and prevent identity fraud**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• E-passports are being introduced in India to enhance the **security and integrity** of travel documents.
 
• They incorporate an **embedded microchip** that stores the passport holder's biometric and personal data, reducing the chances of tampering or identity theft.
 
• The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standards are followed to ensure global acceptance and interoperability of e-passports.
 
• These passports will make the verification process faster and more secure at immigration checkpoints, both domestically and internationally.
 
• The initiative aligns with the Indian government's vision of adopting **cutting-edge technologies** to improve citizen services and foster global mobility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is an e-passport?**

 
 
• An e-passport, also known as a biometric passport, includes an embedded electronic chip that stores the holder's biometric data, such as fingerprints and facial recognition data.
 
• This chip ensures that the passport cannot be easily forged or duplicated.
 
 
 
• **ICAO Standards for E-passports**
 
 
• The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) sets global specifications for the design and functionality of e-passports.
 
• These standards ensure that e-passports are universally recognized and can be scanned at immigration checkpoints worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of E-passports**
 
 
• Enhanced security features to prevent counterfeiting, forgery, and identity theft.
 
• Faster and more efficient immigration checks at airports and border crossings.
 
• Improved trust and acceptance by international authorities for travelers.
 
 
 
• **India's E-passport Initiative**
 
 
• The Indian government plans to introduce e-passports in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs and the Indian Security Press.
 
• These passports will feature advanced security layers and comply with global ICAO guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Role of Biometric Technology**
 
 
• Biometric data stored in e-passports facilitates secure and accurate identification of individuals.
 
• It reduces human errors during verification and enhances the overall efficiency of border control systems.
